headline: 5 questions
body: Use these on anyone selling you something.
punch: Question 3 ends about 80% of arguments instantly.

headline: Question 1
body: Rodents don't undergo true epiphyseal fusion at sexual maturity the way humans do. A mouse growth plate result may not transfer at all.
punch: If they can't tell you the species, they haven't read it.

headline: Question 2
subhead: IN VITRO OR IN A BODY
body: Concentrations in a dish are not doses in a person. Cell culture shows a mechanism can happen, not that it does happen at real exposures.
punch: A dish is not a person.

headline: Question 3
body: This is the big one. Predicted adult height is a model output. Aromatase inhibitor trials improved predicted height in all four studies, and the one that measured actual final height found no difference.
punch: Did anyone measure a finished adult, or just a forecast?

headline: Question 4
body: Loads of the encouraging results in this field come from uncontrolled studies where everyone got treatment. Kids grow anyway. That's what kids do.
punch: Growth without a comparison group proves nothing.

headline: Question 5
body: GH meta-analyses studied kids with idiopathic short stature. Deficiency data comes from deficient patients. Neither group is a person of normal height.
punch: Data about someone else isn't data about you.

headline: The pattern
body: Every one is asking the same thing. Is the evidence actually about the situation you're in, or does it just sound like it is?
punch: Most bad claims are true statements about the wrong population.

headline: And use them on me
body: I've been wrong twice on the growth hormone question in this account, and corrected it publicly both times. Apply the questions to everything, including this.
punch: If the questions only work on other people they're not questions.

headline: It's never over
body: Real mechanisms, real citations, no protocols.
